text: For let the square on one of the sides, $BC$, of triangle $ABC$ be equal to the (sum of the) squares on the sides $BA$ and $AC$. I say that angle $BAC$ is a right-angle.
For let $AD$ have been drawn from point $A$ at right-angles to the straight-line $AC$ [Prop.~1.11],
and let $AD$ have been made equal to $BA$ [Prop.~1.3],
Since $DA$ is equal to $AB$, the square on $DA$ is thus also equal to the square on $AB$.
assertion: the square on DA equals the square on AB

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: square on $DA$ is thus also equal to the square on $AB$

text: Let the square on $AC$ have been added to both.
assertion: the square on AC is added to both sides

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: Let the square on $AC$ have been added to both.

text: Thus, the (sum of the) squares on $DA$ and $AC$ is equal to the (sum of the) squares on $BA$ and $AC$.

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (sum of the) squares on $DA$ and $AC$ is equal to the (sum of the) squares on $BA$ and $AC$

text: But, the (square) on $DC$  is equal to the (sum of the squares) on $DA$ and $AC$. For angle $DAC$ is a right-angle [Prop.~1.47].
assertion: the square on DC equals DA^2 + AC^2

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (square) on $DC$  is equal to the (sum of the squares) on $DA$ and $AC$

text: But, the  (square) on $BC$ is equal to (sum of the squares) on $BA$ and $AC$. For (that) was assumed.
assertion: the square on BC equals BA^2 + AC^2 (the given hypothesis)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (square) on $BC$ is equal to (sum of the squares) on $BA$ and $AC$

text: Thus, the square on $DC$ is equal to the square on $BC$.
assertion: the square on DC equals the square on BC

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: square on $DC$ is equal to the square on $BC$

text: So  side $DC$ is also equal to (side) $BC$.
And since $DA$ is equal to $AB$, and $AC$ (is) common, the two (straight-lines) $DA$, $AC$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $BA$, $AC$.
assertion: the two sides DA, AC equal the two sides BA, AC

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: two (straight-lines) $DA$, $AC$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $BA$, $AC$

text: And the base $DC$ is equal to the base $BC$.

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: base $DC$ is equal to the base $BC$

text: Thus, if the square on one of the sides of a triangle is equal to the (sum of the) squares on the remaining two sides of the triangle then the angle contained by the remaining two sides of the triangle is a right-angle. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
